description: Individuals exposed periconceptionally showed less methylation of the imprinted IGF2 gene six decades later than their own unexposed same-sex siblings. Exposure at the end of pregnancy produced no such difference - the timing is the finding.
energy_note: A mark still readable sixty years later.

description: Prenatal famine exposure is associated with increased risk of schizophrenia and depression in adulthood. Meta-analysis confirms the schizophrenia association; the mediating methylation signal identified is DUSP22, not IGF2 - IGF2 tracks growth and metabolism instead.
energy_note: A psychiatric illness scheduled before birth.

aspect: Genome-scale work replaced the candidate-gene story
description: Malnutrition-associated differentially methylated regions preferentially occur at regulatory regions and map to genes differentially expressed in early development; DMRs in INSR and CPT1A showed enhancer activity and tracked birth weight and LDL cholesterol.
energy_note: Not one gene. A setting across a pathway.

aspect: It is being applied to current sieges
description: Published work now extends the famine-epigenetics framework explicitly to maternal malnutrition in Gaza, on the expectation of the same class of outcome in a cohort currently in utero.
energy_note: A cohort being created now, measurable in 2080.
source_name: ScienceDirect, maternal malnutrition and epigenetics in Gaza

aspect: HONEST LIMIT - the grandchildren claim is not established
description: Heijmans 2008 measured only the directly exposed generation. Assertions that IGF2 methylation changes are inherited into F2 and F3 are extrapolations, not findings. Human transgenerational epigenetic inheritance remains largely unproven.
